# FDGD029

> NOT PERMITTED: Removing a Finalizer from an Unsealed Type

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section D.9.1 Removing a Finalizer from an Unsealed Type. Can cause: runtime break.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Permitted when the finalizer does not use the Basic Dispose Pattern (`Dispose(false)`) or otherwise signal derived types. PublicApiAnalyzers (optional in /fdg-setup) can flag changes to the public API.

## From the book

If an unsealed type has a finalizer implemented by calling `Dispose(false)`, any derived types may have been counting on the call to `Dispose(false)` for their own component of the finalization logic. Removing the finalizer from the base class will thus result in the derived type no longer running finalization logic.

The .NET BCL team considers this an unacceptable breaking change, unless the finalizer does not use the Basic Dispose Pattern or otherwise signal derived types.
